_comment: Climate normals copied from BANDS/SEED_BANDS in camino-itinerary-v13.html (the planner). Baseline period 1991-2020. Used to judge whether an AEMET precipitation/drought anomaly is actually dry FOR THIS STRETCH, rather than dry in the abstract. Keep in sync with the planner.
_use: A drought report is only actionable against a normal. E.g. 'Lleida spring precipitation 40% of normal' means band b4 April fell from ~40 mm to ~16 mm — enough to advance the cereal harvest into the walk window.

b1.name: Basque mountains
b1.station: San Sebastián-Igeldo, adjusted −2–3 °C for interior elevation (weakest station match of the five)

b2.name: Álava plain & Rioja Alavesa
b2.station: Vitoria-Foronda (540 m) — good match for the plain

b4.name: Monegros & Bajo Cinca steppe
b4.station: Zaragoza & Lleida airports — no station in the Monegros interior; real conditions run hotter and drier than either
b4.note: No shade on route. Cierzo (NW wind) 50–70 km/h on ordinary spring days.

b5.name: Catalan interior & Montserrat
b5.station: Lleida; the Igualada–Montserrat stretch is interpolated (moderate confidence)
b5.note: Thunderstorm season begins in May. Montserrat (700 m+) runs several degrees cooler than these valley numbers.

_cereal_note: Cereal-machinery ignition risk concentrates in the Ebro plain (b3), Monegros (b4) and the Lleida plain / Urgell / La Segarra (b5). Normal harvest is mid-June onward, i.e. after a ~20 May finish — a hot, dry spring is what erodes that margin.
